title: Permanent Alimony and Maintenance — Section 25 HMA

content.overview: Section 25 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 provides permanent alimony and maintenance. At the time of any decree or subsequently, the Court may order either spouse to pay the other a gross or periodical sum for maintenance and support, for a term not exceeding the life of the applicant, having regard to incomes, property, conduct and other circumstances. Payment may be secured by a charge on immovable property. The order may be varied on change of circumstances or on remarriage / specified post-decree conduct.
content.glance: Ask: (1) At or after any HMA decree? (2) Either spouse apply? (3) Gross or periodical sum? (4) Factors: means, property, conduct? (5) Variation under (2)/(3)?
content.study:
Section 25(1): at the time of any decree or subsequently, either spouse may apply; Court may order a gross or monthly/periodical sum for a term not exceeding the life of the applicant, having regard to the respondent’s income and property, the applicant’s property, conduct of the parties and other circumstances; payment may be secured by a charge on the respondent’s immovable property.

Section 25(2): variation, modification or rescission on change of circumstances at the instance of either party.

Section 25(3): variation or rescission if the recipient has remarried, or (if the wife) has not remained chaste, or (if the husband) has had sexual intercourse outside wedlock, at the instance of the other party.

Distinct from interim s. 24 and from CrPC s. 125 / BNSS s. 144 and HAMA. Courts coordinate overlapping orders to avoid double recovery.

No case holdings invented. Case-law verification remains a separate gate.

sections.heading: Original order under s. 25(1)
sections.body: At or after any HMA decree; either spouse; gross or periodical sum; factors include means, property, conduct; may secure by charge.

sections.heading: Variation on change of circumstances (s. 25(2))
sections.body: Either party may seek variation, modification or rescission when circumstances of either party change.

sections.heading: Variation on remarriage or specified conduct (s. 25(3))
sections.body: Remarriage of recipient; unchastity of the wife; extramarital intercourse by the husband — other party may seek variation or rescission.

sections.heading: Form and duration
sections.body: Gross or periodical; term not exceeding life of applicant; discretionary and needs-based, not automatic.

sections.heading: Contrast with s. 24
sections.body: s. 24 is pendente lite only; s. 25 is permanent provision at or after the decree.

examples.title: Permanent alimony on divorce
examples.body: Limited-means applicant vs substantial earner after divorce decree — monthly sum under s. 25(1), possibly secured by charge.

examples.title: Rescission after remarriage
examples.body: Recipient remarries — paying party may seek rescission under s. 25(3).

hypotheticals.question: Can a s. 25 order be reduced after the payer loses employment?
hypotheticals.analysis: Yes under s. 25(2) if the Court is satisfied of a change in circumstances and adjusts the sum as appears just.

distinctions.title: s. 25 (permanent) vs s. 24 (interim)
distinctions.left: At or after decree; may last for life of applicant.

rows.right: Ceases on disposal of main proceeding (subject to any s. 25 order).

misconceptions.trap: Permanent alimony can only be a one-time lump sum.
misconceptions.correction: Section 25 permits a gross sum or a monthly/periodical sum, and may secure payment by a charge.

misconceptions.trap: Once made, a s. 25 order cannot be changed.
misconceptions.correction: Sub-sections (2) and (3) expressly permit variation, modification or rescission.
